authority.note: A JSON descriptor rather than YAML so the same bytes are read by the TypeScript contract and an independent Python checker with no new dependency. Every entry here is an interface another project owns. Horizon mints none of them, defines none of their payloads, and cannot grant authority by asserting that one exists. An interface whose owner has not published it is named as an open dependency, and the path that depends on it fails closed until it exists.

interfaces.horizon_view: The owner publishes the decision as a cryptographic envelope, not as a struct: the `godspeed.authority_decision` profile at version 1.0.0, whose `extensions["godspeed.authority_decision"]` names the disposition, the operation, the decision and the committed ledger entry. The envelope is committed to SEA-Forge's ledger as the entry whose `record_kind` is `authority_decision`; that entry's integrity is proved by the ledger's hash chain, by a signed `LedgerCheckpoint`, and by a `MerkleProof` that includes the entry. Horizon reads the envelope, the committed entry and the signed checkpoint. Horizon does not read the in-memory `AuthorityDecision` struct, which carries none of the facts this interface checks, and it does not read a grant: `ActionGrant` is move-only and intentionally not serializable.

horizon_checks: the decision is an Allow before Horizon treats it as authority
the decision names the same operation digest the Horizon record carries
the decision's subject actor is the principal the record names
the envelope's ledger entry is committed and its hash chain verifies
the checkpoint's signature verifies against the owner's trust set at the pinned commit
the checkpoint's Merkle inclusion proof covers the entry the envelope names
interfaces.failure_rule: A decision Horizon cannot resolve against the pinned interface is not authority. The operation is refused; it is never satisfied by a local policy, a session, or a grant. A decision whose signature does not verify against the owner's trust set at the pinned commit is refused whatever it says. The envelope carries no amount and no authority epoch, so Horizon checks the record's amount and epoch against the policy bundle and the trust set the decision names, never against a field the envelope does not have; an artifact that does not carry a fact the record needs is refused, not read around.

interfaces.horizon_view: SEA-Forge mints a grant as a move-only capability and says so: `ActionGrant` is "intentionally not serializable or cloneable" and its fields are private. There is therefore no grant artifact for Horizon to resolve, to check, or to hold, and this interface names what the owner would have to publish before an agent's delegation could be verified independently. Horizon pins no commit, because there is nothing at a commit to point at.

required_facts.meaning: the grant's own identifier, which the delegating record names
the key the owner signed the grant with
the owner's signature over the grant
the hash of the exact action the grant authorizes
the resource scope the grant permits
the spend ceiling the grant permits, with its unit
the authority epoch the grant was issued against
when the grant stops being usable
the committed Allow decision the grant was minted from

horizon_checks: the grant was minted from an Allow decision, never from a Deny or an Escalate
the grant's action hash covers the operation the record carries
the grant's boundaries cover the operation's resource scope
the grant's amount covers the operation's amount in the same unit
the grant's authority epoch is the epoch the trust set names as current
the grant has not expired
the grant carries a signature from a key the owner's trust set names
interfaces.failure_rule: While this interface is unpublished there is no grant artifact to resolve, so the delegated path fails closed: a delegation reference a record carries is a name, not an authority, and the operation is refused. The path never falls back to a session, a local policy, or a human entitlement, and a delegation reference never becomes authority by being asserted.
interfaces.dependency: SEA-Forge owns the grant artifact and publishes none at the pinned revision: `ActionGrant` is a move-only, non-serializable capability, so there is nothing durable for Horizon to verify. Until the owner publishes a grant issuance record carrying the facts above, no agent's delegation can be verified independently and the delegated path refuses.

required_facts.meaning: the entitlement's own identifier
the principal the entitlement was issued to
the authority that issued the entitlement
the key the issuer signed the entitlement with
the issuer's signature over the entitlement
the exact operation the entitlement permits
the resource scope the entitlement covers
the spend ceiling the entitlement grants
the authority epoch the entitlement was issued in
when the entitlement stops being current
whether the entitlement has been revoked

horizon_checks: the entitlement names the same subject as the human it authorizes, through the record kind's own subject field
the entitlement names the same operation digest as the record
the entitlement's resource scope covers every resource the record names
the entitlement's amount covers the record's amount in the same unit
the entitlement carries the same authority epoch as the record
the entitlement expires no earlier than the record it authorizes
the entitlement is active
the entitlement carries the issuer's signature over a key the owner's trust set names
interfaces.horizon_view: The owner may name its payload fields as it likes. Horizon reads the external artifact through an adapter that maps it onto the facts this interface declares; the contract fixes the facts, not the owner's field names. The subject a fact binds to is named per record kind in `subject_binding`, so no fact points at a field that does not exist.
interfaces.failure_rule: While this interface is unpublished the entitlement-backed path is unavailable: every record that names an entitlement is refused, whatever facts it is handed, because an artifact nobody has published cannot be authenticated. When the interface is published, an entitlement that is missing a fact, names a different subject or operation, covers a narrower scope or a smaller amount, carries a different epoch, expires before the record it authorizes, is not active, or is not signed by the issuer the interface names, is refused. The path never falls back to a grant, a session, or a policy decision.
interfaces.dependency: SEA-Forge owns the entitlement artifact and has not published one at the pinned revision. Horizon pins no commit and mints no entitlement. Until the owner publishes an interface that carries every fact above, no human authority may rest on an entitlement, and the governed human path refuses.

bind_targets.record_fields: a field of a Horizon record kind named in contracts/identity/v1/records.json, written as Kind.field

envelope_checks.envelope:profile: the envelope is the godspeed.authority_decision profile and names its own identity, kind, time and producer
envelope_checks.envelope:disposition: the disposition-dependent fields the envelope carries for the decision it reaches
envelope_checks.envelope:ledger_chain: the committed ledger entry, its hash chain and its position in the ledger
envelope_checks.envelope:checkpoint: the signed checkpoint the entry is covered by
envelope_checks.envelope:inclusion: the Merkle inclusion proof of the entry under the checkpoint root

bind_targets.rule: Every required fact names exactly one binds target. A fact Horizon stores binds to a record field; a fact Horizon only uses to verify the owner's artifact binds to an envelope check. Any other target is refused by scripts/check-external-interface-facts.ts.
